title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
methodology: Benchmark methodology: automated LLM- and mutation-based test generation expands HumanEval 80x into HumanEval+; 26 LLMs evaluated.
results: pass@k falls by 19.3-28.9%; rankings change, with WizardCoder-CodeLlama and Phind-CodeLlama beating ChatGPT on HumanEval+ but not on HumanEval.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: CROSSCODEEVAL: A Diverse and Multilingual Benchmark for Cross-File Code Completion
methodology: Benchmark construction: static-analysis-based selection of examples requiring cross-file context in Python, Java, TypeScript and C#; CodeGen and StarCoder evaluated with and without retrieved context.
results: Cross-file context clearly improves completion but performance remains far from solved for the best model; the benchmark also discriminates between context-retrieval methods.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: Personalised Distillation: Empowering Open-Sourced LLMs with Adaptive Learning for Code Generation
methodology: Personalised distillation where the student first attempts the task and the teacher supplies adaptive refinements; only 2.5-3K examples; CodeGen-mono-16B and StarCoder on HumanEval.
results: CodeGen-mono-16B +7% to 36.4% pass@1 and StarCoder +12.2% to 45.8% pass@1, using one third of the data of standard distillation.
venue: EMNLP 2023 - 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings

title: ANPL: Towards Natural Programming with Interactive Decomposition
methodology: Interactive program decomposition system (input-output examples, sketch and natural-language holes) with recursive sub-problem solving; ARC, APPS and HumanEval.
results: Outperforms baseline programming systems that lack interactive decomposition, and is applicable across ARC, APPS, HumanEval and real-world tasks; no figures in the abstract.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: WizardCoder: EMPOWERING CODE LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS WITH EVOL-INSTRUCT
methodology: Code Evol-Instruct instruction fine-tuning; five benchmarks (HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, DS-1000, MultiPL-E).
results: WizardCoder-15B surpasses Claude and Bard on HumanEval/HumanEval+; 34B matches ChatGPT on HumanEval and exceeds it on HumanEval+.
venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024

title: IS SELF-REPAIR A SILVER BULLET FOR CODE GENERATION?
methodology: Cost-aware empirical analysis of self-repair in Code Llama, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on HumanEval and APPS, with feedback-quality ablations and a small human-feedback study.
results: Gains are modest, heterogeneous across subsets and sometimes absent once repair cost is counted; stronger feedback yields larger gains but still trails human-level debugging.
venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024

title: OCTOPACK: INSTRUCTION TUNING CODE LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
methodology: Instruction tuning on CommitPack (4 TB of Git commits, 350 languages) applied to StarCoder 16B; HumanEval and the new HumanEvalPack (repair, explanation, synthesis in six languages).
results: 46.2% pass@1 on HumanEval, state of the art among models not trained on OpenAI outputs; OctoCoder and OctoGeeX lead HumanEvalPack among permissive models.
venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024

title: SWE-BENCH: CAN LANGUAGE MODELS RESOLVE REAL-WORLD GITHUB ISSUES?
methodology: Benchmark construction: 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories requiring repository-level edits; proprietary models and a fine-tuned SWE-Llama evaluated.
results: The best model, Claude 2, resolves only 1.96% of issues; all models solve only the simplest cases.
venue: 12th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2024

title: Magicoder: Empowering Code Generation with OSS-INSTRUCT
methodology: OSS-INSTRUCT synthetic instruction tuning (75K samples) of open models up to 7B; HumanEval+ and other coding benchmarks.
results: MagicoderS-CL-7B reaches 66.5 vs ChatGPT 65.9 pass@1 on HumanEval+.
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

title: EFFI-LEARNER: Enhancing Efficiency of Generated Code via Self-Optimization
methodology: Execution-profile self-optimization loop over 16 open-source and 6 closed-source models on EffiBench, HumanEval and MBPP.
results: StarCoder2-15B execution time 0.93 s to 0.12 s (-87.1%) and total memory 22.02 to 2.03 Mb*s (-90.8%).
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: SelfCodeAlign: Self-Alignment for Code Generation
methodology: Fully self-aligned instruction-tuning pipeline without human labels or distillation; CodeQwen1.5-7B and models from 3B to 33B; HumanEval+ and other benchmarks.
results: 67.1 pass@1 on HumanEval+, beating CodeLlama-70B-Instruct at one tenth the size and outperforming OctoPack and GPT-4o distillation.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: Comments as Natural Logic Pivots: Improve Code Generation via Comment Perspective
methodology: Comment-based contrastive training plus logical comment decoding (MANGO); StarCoder and WizardCoder models from 3B to 7B on HumanEval and MBPP.
results: Significantly improves pass rates over strong baselines and is more robust than chain-of-thought prompting; no figures in the abstract.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Generating Software Tests for Mobile Applications Using Fine-Tuned Large Language Models
methodology: QLoRA supervised fine-tuning of LLaMA 2 13B, Code Llama 13B and Mistral 7B on 16,252 Dart code-test pairs; nine Dart files with 42 test cases in 4-bit and 16-bit precision.
results: TestGen-Dart_v0.2 at 4-bit improves syntactically correct tests by 15.38% and functionally correct tests by 16.67% over Code Llama 13B; also outperforms LLaMA 2 13B and Mistral 7B.
venue: Proceedings - 2024 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automation of Software Test, AST 2024

title: Using Large Language Models to Generate JUnit Tests: An Empirical Study
methodology: Empirical study of JUnit test generation by Codex, GPT-3.5-Turbo and StarCoder on HumanEval and EvoSuite SF110, scoring compilation, correctness, coverage and test smells.
results: Codex exceeds 80% coverage on HumanEval, but no model exceeds 2% on EvoSuite SF110; generated tests show duplicated asserts and empty tests.
venue: ACM International Conference Proceeding Series

title: Test-Driven Development and LLM-based Code Generation
methodology: Controlled prompt experiment adding test cases to problem statements; GPT-4 and Llama 3 on MBPP and HumanEval.
results: Including tests consistently improves success rates; no overall figure reported in the abstract.
venue: Proceedings - 2024 39th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2024

title: Sifting through the Chaff: On Utilizing Execution Feedback for Ranking the Generated Code Candidates
methodology: Multi-task code ranker (RankEF) combining classification with execution-feedback generation; APPS, MBPP and HumanEval.
results: Relative Pass@1/Pass@2/Pass@5 improvements of +30.97%, +31.43% and +19.51% on APPS over CodeRanker.
venue: Proceedings - 2024 39th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2024

title: PREFERENCE OPTIMIZATION FOR REASONING WITH PSEUDO FEEDBACK
methodology: Preference optimization with test-case-based pseudo feedback, from frontier models or extended self-consistency; Mathstral-7B and DeepSeek-coder-7B on MATH, GSM8K and LiveCodeBench.
results: MATH 58.3 to 68.6, GSM8K 85.6 to 90.3, College Math 34.3 to 42.3; LiveCodeBench 21.1 to 24.3, surpassing Claude-3-Haiku.
venue: 13th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2025

title: Unraveling the Potential of Large Language Models in Code Translation: How Far are We?
methodology: Large-scale empirical study of code translation with PolyHumanEval (14 languages) and over 110,000 translations, plus intermediary translation and self-training; CodeLlama-13B.
results: Python-to-other translation improves by 11.7% on average in computation accuracy; Go emerges as a useful intermediary language.
venue: Proceedings - Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference, APSEC

title: Guided Code Generation with LLMs: A Multi-Agent Framework for Complex Code Tasks
methodology: Multi-agent guided code generation with fine-grained task decomposition; Llama 3.1 8B at int4 precision on HumanEval.
results: 23.79% improvement in solution accuracy over direct one-shot generation.
venue: Proceedings of the 12th International Japan-Africa Conference on Electronics, Communications, and Computations, JAC-ECC 2024

title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
methodology: SWE-Gym training environment with 2,438 executable task instances; fine-tuned SWE agents plus inference-time verifiers; SWE-bench Verified and Lite.
results: Up to +19% absolute resolution rate; 32.0% on Verified and 26.0% on Lite with verifiers, state of the art for open-weight SWE agents.
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

title: RECODE: Leveraging Reliable Self-generated Tests and Fine-Grained Execution Feedback to Enhance LLM-Based Code Generation
methodology: Inference-time framework: self-generated test cross-validation, static pattern extraction, CFG-based execution debugging; five LLMs including Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on HumanEval/MBPP.
results: Pass@1 +5.82% average; static patterns +5.40% on HumanEval; CFG debugging up to +13.9%.
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science

title: Efficient Beam Search for LLMs Using Trie-Based Decoding
methodology: Trie-based parallel decoding sharing one KV cache across beams; Phi-3.5-mini, Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-Small-24B on CNN/DailyMail and HumanEval.
results: 4-8x memory savings and up to 2.4x faster decoding with no quality loss.
venue: EMNLP 2025 - 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings of the Conference

title: Thinking Before Running! Efficient Code Generation with Thorough Exploration and Optimal Refinement
methodology: Exploration-plus-refinement framework with Reinforced Self-Training preference optimization; HumanEval and MBPP against MapCoder and AgentCoder.
results: Pass@1 +3.0% over MapCoder at 6.4% of its compute; +0.5% over AgentCoder in 2 versus 5 rounds; LLaMA2-7B competitive at 20% of the compute.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: SEK: Self-Explained Keywords Empower Large Language Models for Code Generation
methodology: Self-explained-keywords prompting: the model extracts and explains under-trained terms before generating code; five LLMs on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), APPS and BigCodeBench.
results: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct improves from 85.4% to 93.3% Pass@1 on HumanEval, with consistent gains across benchmarks.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: AlphaVerus: Bootstrapping Formally Verified Code Generation througSelf-Improving Translation and Treefinement
methodology: Self-improving framework with translation exploration, verifier-guided Treefinement search and filtering of misaligned specifications; LLaMA-3.1-70B on HumanEval and MBPP without fine-tuning.
results: Generates formally verified solutions for HumanEval and MBPP without human intervention or model fine-tuning; no pass rates given.
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

title: Tree-of-Evolution: Tree-Structured Instruction Evolution for Code Generation in Large Language Models
methodology: Tree-structured instruction evolution (Tree-of-Evolution) with optimization-driven refinement; 75K synthesized samples; HumanEval, MBPP, EvalPlus, LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench.
results: Models fine-tuned on 75K ToE samples match or exceed Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct, which was trained on millions of samples.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Post-Training Performance Boosting Method for Code Large Language Models via Model Merging
methodology: Bayesian Auto Merging: model merging of pre- and post-SFT checkpoints with Bayesian hyperparameter search; Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder on HumanEval and MBPP.
results: Average pass@1 +1.6% on HumanEval, recovering capability lost to catastrophic forgetting after SFT.
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science

title: Dynamic Scaling of Unit Tests for Code Reward Modeling
methodology: Unit-test scaling for code reward modeling with a lightweight test generator (CodeRM-8B) and difficulty-adaptive dynamic scaling; HumanEval+.
results: +18.43% for Llama3-8B and +3.42% for GPT-4o-mini on HumanEval+, with larger benefits on harder problems.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: S∗: Test Time Scaling for Code Generation
methodology: Hybrid parallel plus sequential test-time scaling with adaptively generated distinguishing inputs; 12 LLMs and reasoning models; LiveCodeBench.
results: A 3B model outperforms GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4o-mini with S* beats o1-preview by 3.7%; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B reaches 85.7% versus o1 at 88.5%.
venue: EMNLP 2025 - 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Findings of EMNLP 2025

title: SeedLoRA: A Fusion Approach to Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
methodology: Two-stage fusion of LoRA adapters trained with different random seeds on a single task; LLaMA2-7B and Mistral-7B on GSM8K and HumanEval.
results: +4.9% on GSM8K and +6.6% on HumanEval over individual LoRA models, matching or exceeding full fine-tuning.
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

title: KODCODE: A Diverse, Challenging, and Verifiable Synthetic Dataset for Coding
methodology: Synthetic dataset construction with question-solution-test triplets, self-verification and reject sampling from DeepSeek-R1 (KODCODE); SFT evaluated on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench.
results: KODCODE-tuned models reach state-of-the-art results, surpassing Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B; no figures in the abstract.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: ACECODER: Acing Coder RL via Automated Test-Case Synthesis
methodology: Automated test-case synthesis to build preference pairs and reward models (Bradley-Terry) plus RL with test-pass rewards (AceCoder); Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench.
results: Best-of-32 gains of about 10 points for Llama-3.1-8B and 5 points for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, putting the 7B model on par with 236B DeepSeek-V2.5; RL adds over 25% on HumanEval+ and 6% on MBPP+ in 80 steps.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Efficient Model Development through Fine-tuning Transfer
methodology: Fine-tuning transfer by extracting and applying parameter diff vectors across model versions; Llama 3.0 8B to Llama 3.1 8B, measured on IFEval, LiveCodeBench and Global MMLU.
results: +46.9% on IFEval and +15.7% on LiveCodeBench without further training, surpassing Llama 3.1 8B Instruct; multilingual gains of 4.7% (Malagasy) and 15.5% (Turkish).
venue: EMNLP 2025 - 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings of the Conference

title: Concept Distillation from Strong to Weak Models via Hypotheses-to-Theories Prompting
methodology: Automatic prompt optimization via concept distillation: collect weak-model mistakes, induce rules with a strong model, verify and integrate them; NL2Code and mathematical reasoning with Mistral-7B and Phi-3-mini.
results: Mistral-7B accuracy +20% on Multi-Arith and Phi-3-mini-3.8B accuracy +34% on HumanEval.
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Annual Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies: Long Papers, NAACL-HLT 2025

title: EcoTune: Token-Efficient Multi-Fidelity Hyperparameter Optimization for Large Language Model Inference
methodology: Token-efficient multi-fidelity hyperparameter optimization for inference settings, with token-based fidelity and a token-aware acquisition function; LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3 on MMLU, HumanEval, MedQA and OpenBookQA.
results: Improves over the HELM leaderboard by 7.1%, 24.3%, 21.9% and 4.6% while cutting token consumption by over 80%.
venue: EMNLP 2025 - 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Proceedings of the Conference

title: Assessing Dialect Fairness and Robustness of Large Language Models in Reasoning Tasks
methodology: Construction of ReDial, 1.2K+ parallel Standardized English and AAVE query pairs rewriting seven benchmarks including HumanEval; evaluation of GPT, Claude, Llama, Mistral and Phi families.
results: Almost all evaluated models show significant brittleness and unfairness on AAVE queries across reasoning tasks.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Large Language Model-Aware In-Context Learning for Code Generation
methodology: LLM-aware demonstration selection for in-context learning (LAIL), training a retriever on model-labeled positive and negative examples; four LLMs, five datasets including DevEval.
results: Pass@1 gains of 11.58%, 3.33% and 5.07% for CodeGen-Multi-16B and 10.04% on DevEval for CodeLlama-7B over state-of-the-art baselines.
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

title: Improving FIM Code Completions via Context & Curriculum Based Learning
methodology: Context- and curriculum-based fine-tuning for fill-in-the-middle completion; StarCoder and DeepSeek models on SantaCoder FIM, Amazon CCEval and a new multi-line infilling benchmark.
results: Gains are larger for smaller models; online A/B testing improves completion acceptance and persistence rates with no latency cost.
venue: WSDM 2025 - Proceedings of the 18th ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining

title: Fully Autonomous Programming Using Iterative Multi-Agent Debugging with Large Language Models
methodology: Multi-agent synthesize-execute-instruct-debug-repair framework (SEIDR) with lexicase and tournament selection; PSB2 and HumanEval-X; GPT-3.5 and Llama 3.
results: SEIDR solves 18 PSB2 problems in C++ and 20 in Python; Llama 3-8B reaches 84.2% average pass@100 on HumanEval-C++; 163/164 and 162/164 problems solved at least once with GPT-3.5 and Llama 3-8B.
venue: ACM Transactions on Evolutionary Learning and Optimization

title: Collaboration between intelligent agents and large language models: A novel approach for enhancing code generation capability
methodology: Four-stage multi-agent pipeline with a fine-tuned BART prompt generator; HumanEval, MBPP and LLMSecEval with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
results: Pass@1 +18.9% and +23.2% vs GPT-3.5; logical error rate 38.2%/29.1% to 19.3%/13.6%; GPT-4 +16.9% pass@1 and secure@1 48.6% to 55.3%.
venue: Expert Systems with Applications

title: InverseCoder: Self-improving Instruction-Tuned Code LLMs with Inverse-Instruct
methodology: Inverse-Instruct data augmentation, generating additional instructions for existing code responses from the model's own training data; CodeLlama-Python and DeepSeek-Coder on HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), DS-1000 and MultiPL-E.
results: Consistently improves base models across benchmarks; no figures in the abstract.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Locally-deployed Open-source LLMs for Code Generation: Promises and Challenges
methodology: Evaluation of six open-source LLMs on HumanEval across five prompting techniques (zero-shot, test-driven, chain-of-thought, MapCoder, LLM-Debugger).
results: Code-specialized models with advanced debugging reach up to 88.02% pass@1, described as rivaling cloud-based solutions.
venue: PAIS 2025 - Proceeding: 7th International Conference on Pattern Analysis and Intelligent Systems

title: Template-Guided Program Repair in the Era of Large Language Models
methodology: Two-stage neural template repair: fine-tuned million-level model for template selection plus fine-tuned billion-level model for patch generation; Defects4J v1.2 and HumanEval-Java.
results: StarCoder fixes 128 and 129 bugs (+14 and +59 over the best baseline); CodeLlama fixes 139 and 136 (+25 and +66).
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Software Engineering

title: PerfCodeGen: Improving Performance of LLM Generated Code with Execution Feedback
methodology: Training-free execution-feedback self-refinement loop; open-weight models (Phi-3-mini, Llama 3 8B, Mixtral 8x7B, Command R, Llama 3 70B) on HumanEval, MBPP and APPS.
results: Speedups on a larger share of problems than strong prompting; Phi-3-mini matches naive GPT-4 optimization rates; often beats reference solutions.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE/ACM 2nd International Conference on AI Foundation Models and Software Engineering, FORGE 2025

title: Code Ranking with Structure Awareness Contrastive Learning
methodology: Structure-aware contrastive learning ranker (SACL-CR) for selecting the best of multiple sampled programs; CodeLlama and DeepSeekCoder on HumanEval and MBPP.
results: Reports significant pass@k gains over ranker-based selection baselines; no figures given in the abstract.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Program Comprehension

title: Guided Search Strategies in Non-Serializable Environments with Applications to Software Engineering Agents
methodology: Guided test-time search (one-step lookahead and trajectory selection with a learned action-value estimator) for non-serializable environments; SWE-bench Verified with fine-tuned Qwen-72B and GPT-4o.
results: Success rate doubles to 40.8% for fine-tuned Qwen-72B, state of the art among open-weight models; similar gains transfer to GPT-4o.
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research

title: UCP: a unified framework for code generation with pseudocode-based multi-task learning and reinforcement alignment
methodology: Pseudocode-based multi-task fine-tuning plus RL alignment and multi-granularity completion data; post-training Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct.
results: HumanEval pass@1 84.15% to 87.80%; LiveCodeBench 25.4% to 27.2%.
venue: Journal of Supercomputing

title: Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models
methodology: Type-constrained decoding using prefix automata and search over inhabitable types, formalized on a simply-typed language and extended to TypeScript; HumanEval and MBPP.
results: Compilation errors reduced by more than half and functional correctness significantly increased across model sizes and families, including open-weight models above 30B.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages

title: The Art of Repair: Optimizing Iterative Program Repair with Instruction-Tuned Models
methodology: APR pipeline balancing multi-output generation and iterative repair with a 10-patch budget; DeepSeekCoder-Instruct, CodeLlama-Instruct and Llama3.1-Instruct fine-tuned at 1K/30K/65K with full fine-tuning or LoRA; HumanEval-Java and Defects4J.
results: Using under 1% of the fine-tuning data yields up to 78% more plausible patches; returns diminish past a data threshold; iteration helps most on complex benchmarks.
venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering , EASE, 2025 edition, EASE 2025

title: From Prompts to Properties: Rethinking LLM Code Generation with Property-Based Testing
methodology: Property-based testing as a complement to unit tests; StarCoder and CodeLlama evaluated on MBPP and HumanEval.
results: 30-32% of solutions only partially satisfy properties and 18-23% fail outright; 9-13% of constraints missed, so pass@k overestimates correctness.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGSOFT Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering

title: Comparative Analysis of Pre-trained Code Language Models for Automated Program Repair via Code Infill Generation
methodology: Systematic evaluation of 20 pre-trained code language models (60M to 16B) on HumanEval-Java (163 buggy methods), measuring accuracy, resource use, compilability, patch diversity and sampling strategy.
results: CodeLLaMA-13B and StarCoder fix the most bugs; scale alone does not guarantee effectiveness (CodeGen2 underperforms); nucleus sampling slightly beats beam search without statistical significance.
venue: GPCE 2025 - Proceedings of the 24th ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Generative Programming: Concepts and Experiences

title: Bridging the Language Gap: Enhancing Multilingual Prompt-Based Code Generation in LLMs via Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer
methodology: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer projecting LASER embeddings into the LLM token space; CodeLlama and CodeGemma on a translated MBPP set.
results: Substantial MBPP quality gains for non-English prompts; prompt translation, data augmentation and fine-tuning prove insufficient, but no figures are given.
venue: Proceedings of the International Joint Conference on Neural Networks

title: Enhancing LLM-Based Code Generation with Complexity Metrics: A Feedback-Driven Approach
methodology: Empirical analysis of complexity metrics versus Pass@1 with logistic regression, then iterative complexity-aware feedback prompting; GPT-4o, GPT-3.5 Turbo, Llama 3.1 and o3-mini on HumanEval, MBPP, LeetCode and BigCodeBench.
results: GPT-3.5 Turbo Pass@1 +35.71% versus +12.5% for the baseline on HumanEval; with Reflexion, +20% (GPT-4o) and +23.07% (o3-mini).
venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE 49th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference, COMPSAC 2025

title: QSpark: Towards Reliable Qiskit Code Generation
methodology: RL fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Coder-32B with GRPO vs ORPO on annotated synthetic Qiskit data; Qiskit HumanEval and HumanEval.
results: ORPO 56.29% Pass@1 on Qiskit HumanEval (+~10 pp over Granite-8B-QK), GRPO 49%; HumanEval 65.90% and 63.00%; neither solves any of the five advanced tasks.
venue: CEUR Workshop Proceedings

title: Implementation of System Code Generation Based on Large Language Model Fine-tune with QLoRA
methodology: QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct on CodeExercise-Python27k and Tested-22k-Python-Alpaca; HumanEval and HumanEval+.
results: Pass@1 +7.3% on HumanEval and +4.3% on HumanEval+ over the base model.
venue: 2025 International Conference on Information and Communication Technology, ICoICT 2025

title: RepairLLaMA: Efficient Representations and Fine-Tuned Adapters for Program Repair
methodology: Program repair adapters with repair-specific code representations and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (RepairLLaMA); Defects4J v2, HumanEval-Java and GitBug-Java.
results: Correctly fixes 144 Defects4J v2, 109 HumanEval-Java and 20 GitBug-Java bugs, outperforming all baselines.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering

title: SRA-MCTS: Self-driven Reasoning Augmentation with Monte Carlo Tree Search for Code Generation
methodology: Monte Carlo Tree Search self-generated reasoning traces with iterative self-evaluation, used as SFT data; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and two other scales; MBPP-Complex and related benchmarks.
results: +11 points on MBPP-Complex for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with consistent gains across three model scales and no extra supervision.
venue: IJCAI International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Advancements in AI-Powered Code Generation: A Comparative Analysis of Modern LLMs
methodology: Narrative comparative analysis of eight code LLMs (CodeGeex, CodeLlama, StarCoder, PanGu-Coder, WizardCoder, CodeT5+, DeepSeek-Coder, CodeGen-Mono) using HumanEval/MBPP pass@1 and pass@100.
results: PanGu-Coder, WizardCoder and DeepSeek-Coder lead general-purpose generation, while CodeLlama and CodeGen-Mono excel on Python; no new experiments reported.
venue: Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications, ICIMIA 2025

title: The Impact of Fine-Tuning Large Language Models on Automated Program Repair
methodology: Controlled comparison of no fine-tuning vs full fine-tuning vs LoRA/IA3 across six code LLMs (CodeGen, CodeT5, StarCoder, DeepSeekCoder, Bloom, CodeLlama2) on QuixBugs, Defects4J and HumanEval-Java.
results: Full fine-tuning degrades benchmark performance through distribution shift and overfitting; parameter-efficient methods (LoRA, IA3) give better repair results.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution, ICSME 2025

title: A Taxonomy of Inefficiencies in LLM-Generated Python Code
methodology: Manual analysis of 492 HumanEval+ snippets from CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder and CodeGemma, producing a taxonomy validated by a survey of 58 practitioners.
results: Taxonomy of 5 categories and 19 subcategories; logic and performance inefficiencies are the most frequent and often co-occur.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution, ICSME 2025

title: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models: Case Study of GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek
methodology: Descriptive comparative case study of Gemini 2.0 Pro, DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT using MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench and MATH-500 (Feb 2025 snapshot).
results: Qualitative comparison of architecture, features and response time; no quantitative results in the abstract.
venue: 2025 13th International Scientific Conference on Computer Science, COMSCI 2025 - Proceedings

title: DR-CoT: dynamic recursive chain of thought with meta reasoning for parameter efficient models
methodology: Inference framework combining recursive reasoning, dynamic context truncation and voting; parameter-efficient models on GPQA Diamond, AIME2024 and HumanEval.
results: GPQA +1.5% (Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking), +2.7% (Grok 3), +4.4% (o3-mini); AIME +3-4 pp; on HumanEval claims gains over Llama 70B, Phi-3 and Claude Sonnet without figures.
venue: Scientific Reports

title: H1B-KV: Hybrid One-Bit Caches for Memory-Efficient Large Language Model Inference
methodology: Hybrid KV-cache compression (1-bit key sketches, 4-bit values) plus lightweight fine-tuning; 7B model on GSM8K, MMLU and HumanEval.
results: An 8k-token context fits in under 60 MB of cache (70x reduction) while matching full-precision quality on all three tasks.
venue: 2025 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference, URTC 2025 - Conference Proceedings

title: CodeSync: Multi-Agent System for Programming Assistance and Deterministic Thinking
methodology: Multi-agent system (facilitator plus thinking, planning, execution, validation and evaluation agents) with strict decoding; Llama-4-maverick on HumanEval and MBPP.
results: 87.4% on HumanEval and 91.2% on MBPP, claimed to outperform existing multi-agent systems without a strong reasoning model.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Metaverse and Cybersecurity, ICAMAC 2025

title: Evaluating Readability and Accessibility of Code Generated by Large Language Models
methodology: Prompt-engineering comparison (baseline vs style-constrained) on 15 HumanEval+ tasks; DeepSeek-R1-0528 and gpt-oss-20b-Q2; pytest correctness plus Pylint style.
results: Average Pylint score 4.09 to 6.41 for DeepSeek-R1-0528 and 6.14 to 8.13 for gpt-oss-20b-Q2.
venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Scientific and Technical Conference Actual Problems of Electronic Instrument Engineering, APEIE 2025

title: MCTS-Refined CoT: High-Quality Fine-Tuning Data for LLM-Based Repository Issue Resolution
methodology: MCTS-based chain-of-thought data generation with reflective rejection sampling and step verification; fine-tuned Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct; SWE-bench Lite and Verified.
results: 28.3% (Lite) and 35.0% (Verified) resolution vs 24.7%/32.8% for SWE-Fixer-Qwen-72B; 43.8% on Verified when issue locations are provided.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2025

title: Effective Code Membership Inference for Code Completion Models via Adversarial Prompts
methodology: Adversarial-prompt membership inference attack with a trained classifier over output variations; Code Llama 7B on APPS and HumanEval.
results: AUC gains of up to 102% over state-of-the-art membership-inference baselines, with strong cross-model and cross-dataset transferability.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2025

title: SemGuard: Real-Time Semantic Evaluator for Correcting LLM-Generated Code
methodology: Semantic-evaluator-driven decoding: a line-level evaluator trained on SemDiff flags semantic deviations on partial code and triggers rollback and regeneration; CodeLlama-7B, StarCoder2-7B and DeepSeekCoder-6.7B across four benchmarks.
results: Semantic error rate falls 19.86% vs ROCODE on SemDiff; Pass@1 rises 48.92% on LiveCodeBench with CodeLlama-7B, with gains transferring to other models and languages.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2025

title: Automated Repair of Ambiguous Problem Descriptions for LLM-Based Code Generation
methodology: Ambiguity repair via program-distribution testing and repair plus contrastive specification inference (SPEC-FIX); GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B on HumanEval+, MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench.
results: 43.58% of descriptions were modified, improving Pass@1 by 30.9% on the modified set and 4.09% absolute overall; repairs transfer across models by 10.48%.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2025

title: Issue Localization via LLM-Driven Iterative Code Graph Searching
methodology: Two-phase code graph search for function-level issue localization with a pruner and reflection mechanism (COSIL); SWE-bench Lite and Verified with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B.
results: Top-1 localization accuracy of 43.3% (Lite) and 44.6% (Verified), 96.04% above prior state of the art; integrated into Agentless, resolution improves by 2.98% to 30.5%.
venue: Proceedings - 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, ASE 2025

title: Specializing LLMs for Code: A Framework for Efficient Adaptation and Robust Evaluation
methodology: PEFT specialization of Llama 3.1 8B on synthetic plus expert-curated data; evaluated on a new post-training-cutoff LeetCode benchmark and on HumanEval.
results: 39.3% pass@1 on the novel benchmark, +23.5 pp over the base model, while gains on the saturated HumanEval are modest.
venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models, FLLM 2025

title: Investigating Retrieval Augmented Generation for LLM-Based Code Generation
methodology: Systematic RAG variants plus self-evaluation on Qwen2.5-Coder; MBPP+.
results: RAG improves pass@1 by up to 10.11% over baseline, with self-evaluation adding further gains on edge cases and logical errors.
venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models, FLLM 2025

title: Holistic evaluation of LLM-Based Code Generation
methodology: Holistic evaluation of four general-purpose LLMs (Llama3-70b, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4.1-nano, Llama4-maverick) on HumanEval, MBPP, APPS and Mercury Beyond, measuring correctness, runtime efficiency and maintainability.
results: Performance differences depend strongly on the benchmark; GPT-4.1-nano is runtime-efficient but weak on maintainability, motivating multi-dimensional evaluation.
venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models, FLLM 2025

title: Efficient LLM Tuning: A Multi-Objective Approach for Code Generation
methodology: Multi-objective hyperparameter optimization with NSGA-II, co-optimizing inference parameters and prompting strategies; Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Mistral-7B on HumanEval.
results: Pareto-optimal configurations beat a sequential-search baseline on accuracy while cutting optimization time by 6x to 12x.
venue: 2025 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems, WCNPS 2025

title: Piloting Copilot, Codex, and StarCoder2: Hot temperature, cold prompts, or black magic?
methodology: Factorial experiment varying prompt, context, temperature and sample count across Copilot, Codex and StarCoder2; HumanEval and LeetCode.
results: Up to 79.27% one-shot success vs 22.44% (Codex) and 31.1% (Copilot) at default settings; optimal settings vary per problem and replicate on StarCoder2.
venue: Journal of Systems and Software

title: Condor: A Code Discriminator Integrating General Semantics With Code Details
methodology: Contrastive-learning code discriminator (Condor) enriched with intermediate code-modification data; CodeNanoFix, APPS, MBPP and LiveCodeBench.
results: Discriminative F1 67% to 73% for DeepSeek-Coder 1.3B; Llama-3.1-70B Pass@1 52.64% to 62.63% on CodeNanoFix and +147.05% on APPS.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering

title: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Prioritization and Cognitive Validation
methodology: Multi-agent framework with test-case prioritization and a cognitive validation loop; DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen2.5-Coder and Llama-3.1 on HumanEval-ET and MBPP-ET.
results: Claims consistent gains over state-of-the-art baselines in correctness and efficiency; no numbers given in the abstract.
venue: Proceedings - Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference, APSEC

title: Meta-analysis of large language models: benchmarking DeepSeek-R1 against ChatGPT, Gemini, Qwen, and LLaMA
methodology: Hybrid meta-analysis aggregating public benchmarks, model cards, technical reports and repositories; MMLU, HumanEval, FLORES-200 and TyDiQA plus efficiency KPIs.
results: DeepSeek-R1 80.2 +/- 1.5% on HumanEval and 78.5 +/- 1.8% on MMLU vs ChatGPT-4 Turbo 86.5 +/- 1.9%; heterogeneity I2 = 14.6%.
venue: Journal of Big Data

title: Enhancing JavaScript Code Autocompletion by Fine-Tuning StarCoder
methodology: Fine-tuning StarCoder-15B on a curated Stack-v2 subset targeting hard prediction cases; evaluated on HumanEval-X JavaScript.
results: pass@1 of 34.4 points after fine-tuning, an improvement over the base model.
venue: Lecture Notes in Electrical Engineering

title: Residual Feature Enhancement for Large Language Models: Methodology and Applications
methodology: Lightweight residual feature enhancement module (linear transform, SwiGLU, residual connections) added to ChatGLM4-9B; six benchmarks including MBPP.
results: MBPP 56.82% vs 55.02% for adapter-based tuning; ablations show up to 3.84 pp degradation when the module is removed.
venue: IEEE Access

title: Distributed Modularization of Thought: Lets Small Rival Large LMs
methodology: Multiple small models fine-tuned per subtask and coordinated through hierarchical multi-level reasoning graphs, distilled from ChatGPT-4.1 with quantized LoRA; BigCodeBench.
results: A system of specialized small models beats single-model baselines on pass@1 and CodeBLEU, claimed to rival larger models.
venue: IEEE Access

title: MACE: Modular Adaptive Code Engine with Context-Aware LoRA Expert Routing and Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
methodology: Context-aware LoRA expert routing, three-level hierarchical RAG and a multi-signal verification loop; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on 25 curated problems plus 50 HumanEval tasks.
results: 35% average generation speedup (43% on hard problems) and correctness 84% to 96%, +12 pp over the base model, trained on a single consumer GPU.
venue: CEUR Workshop Proceedings

title: Performance analysis of AI-generated code: A case study of Copilot, Copilot Chat, CodeLlaMa, and DeepSeek-Coder models
methodology: Static and dynamic performance-regression analysis of Copilot, Copilot Chat, CodeLlama and DeepSeek-Coder on HumanEval, AixBench, MBPP and EvalPerf, with few-shot and CoT prompt interventions.
results: Functionally correct code frequently regresses in performance; four root causes and eleven subcategories identified; root-cause-grounded few-shot prompting helps while CoT is less effective or harmful.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering

title: TDPGen: Optimizing Agentic Code Generation via Test-Driven Planning and Hierarchical ReAct
methodology: Multi-agent architecture combining a test agent, test-driven planning and hierarchical ReAct; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, MBPP, MBPP-ET and APPS.
results: Pass@1 +10.4% on HumanEval and +16.2% on MBPP over established baselines.
venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology, ISCAIT 2026

title: Disentangling Intrinsic Importance from Emergent Structure in Multi-Expert Orchestration
methodology: Interpretability analysis (INFORM) of multi-expert orchestration, decoupling routing structure, execution order and gradient-based functional attribution; ten 8B experts on GSM8K, HumanEval and MMLU.
results: Routing dominance is a poor proxy for functional necessity: frequently routed experts can be interaction hubs with little influence, and masking intrinsically important experts collapses the interaction structure.
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research

title: Evaluating LLMs for Source Code Generation and Summarization Using Machine Learning Classification and Ranking
methodology: Machine-learning feature analysis (SVM classification, RankNet ranking) over outputs of four open LLMs (Mistral, CodeLlama, Gemma 2, Phi-3) on MBPP.
results: 49% maximum classification accuracy, 86% AUC, 90% precision and 92% recall; Gemma 2 leads summarization ranking with a 1.93 win probability and Phi-3 follows at 1.66.
venue: Computers

title: CodeUltraFeedback: An LLM-as-a-Judge Dataset for Aligning Large Language Models to Coding Preferences
methodology: LLM-as-a-judge dataset (10k instructions, 14 LLMs); SFT + RLAIF/DPO alignment of CodeLlama-7B-Instruct; HumanEval+ evaluation.
results: Alignment +22.7%/+29.7% under GPT-3.5/GPT-4 judges; +10.5% Pass@1 and +26.6% Pass@10 (relative) on HumanEval+; beats CodeLlama-13B/34B on coding preferences.
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

title: An exploratory study on fine-tuning large language models for secure code generation
methodology: Full fine-tuning vs LoRA vs IA3 on four code LLMs; 14,622 C/C++ vulnerability-fix files; 52 CWE security scenarios plus HumanEval_CPP.
results: Security +6.4% (C) and +5.0% (C++); LoRA beats prompt-based baselines; function- and block-level data best; CodeLlama Pass@1 +2% on HumanEval_CPP with no correctness loss.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering

title: Steer Your Model: Secure Code Generation With Contrastive Decoding
methodology: Two-stage security steering: functional tuning plus a plug-and-play steering matrix and contrastive decoding; StarCoder, Qwen2.5-Coder and CodeLlama on 60 security scenarios plus HumanEval/MBPP.
results: Security +28.09% vs original models, +12.07% vs CoSec, +4.82% vs SVEN; functional correctness +55.03% on HumanEval and +41.81% on MBPP.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering

title: Multimodal Approaches for Efficient Evaluation of Handwritten Answer Scripts via Large Language Models
methodology: Visual question-answering over handwritten exam scripts with Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama 3.2 Vision, Mistral Vision and Qwen-2VL, plus regex-based answer segmentation and semantic embedding scoring.
results: Claims state-of-the-art grading performance, but the abstract cites unrelated coding and math benchmarks and reports no grading metrics; results not verifiable from the abstract.
venue: Proceedings of International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond, NQComp 2026

title: Self-Guided Planning and Repair Framework for Code Generation (Student Abstract)
methodology: Self-guided planning and repair framework with a plan database, a learned strategy selector and multi-round repair; Llama-3 8B/70B and GPT-4o-mini, trained on HumanEval and tested on MBPP.
results: Pass@1 +4.9% on HumanEval and +5.5% on MBPP over Modularization-of-Thought prompting.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Programming Language Confusion: When Code LLMs Can't Keep Their Languages Straight
methodology: Systematic evaluation of programming-language confusion across 10 LLMs and six multilingual datasets (LiveCodeBench, BabelCode variants, HumanEval-XL, McEval).
results: Confusion is frequent and systematic, with a strong default to Python and migrations between similar languages; explicit language keywords mitigate best; quantization amplifies confusion.
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering, SANER 2026

title: Compute-Optimal Resource Allocation for Distributed Large Language Model Inference in Cloud-Scale Intelligent Systems
methodology: Compute-optimal distributed inference with test-time scaling: difficulty estimator, hierarchical scheduling and elastic cluster scaling (AdaptiScale); Mistral-7B on A4000 GPUs over GSM8K, MATH and HumanEval.
results: 20% higher throughput and 2.1x better cost-efficiency than static best-of-16; 67.2% on GSM8K and cost down from $0.85 to $0.52 per 1000 requests.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security, ISDFS

title: Code generation with large language models: a survey from neural program synthesis to autonomous software development
methodology: Narrative survey covering program synthesis from rule-based methods to autonomous agents, including architectures, training, evaluation, security and ethics.
results: HumanEval pass@1 spans a wide range across model generations; the authors stress contamination and protocol differences and report no new measurements.
venue: Applied Intelligence

title: Not All Local LLMs Are Equal: A Benchmark of Energy and Performance
methodology: Energy and performance benchmark of five local LLMs on HumanEval-X and MBPP+ under CPU-only inference, comparing 0-shot and 3-shot prompting.
results: Clear accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across models; 3-shot prompting improves runtime and energy without hurting code quality.
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE/ACM 10th International Workshop on Green and Sustainable Software, GREENS 2026

title: Beyond Public Benchmarks: An LLM-as-Judge Framework for Enterprise Code Evaluation with Margin-Driven Optimization
methodology: Triadic evaluation (public benchmarks + private repository tasks + complexity-aware scoring) with joint cross-entropy and margin-loss optimization; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen3-8B.
results: 51.8% performance differential: 74.1% mean on HumanEval/MBPP vs 22.3% on private tasks; Qwen3-8B scores 63.4% on HumanEval but 2.8% on private tasks; joint loss gives +32.5% and +41% aggregate gains.
venue: Proceedings - 2026 1st International Workshop on AI for Software Quality Evaluation: Judgment, Metrics, Benchmarks, and Beyond, AI-SQE 2026

title: SWEnergy: An Empirical Study on Energy Efficiency in Agentic Issue Resolution Frameworks with SLMs
methodology: Controlled evaluation of four agentic issue-resolution frameworks (SWE-Agent, OpenHands, Mini SWE Agent, AutoCodeRover) with Gemma-3 4B and Qwen-3 1.7B on SWE-bench Verified Mini; 150 runs per configuration measuring energy, time, tokens and memory.
results: AutoCodeRover consumes 9.4x more energy than OpenHands; resolution rates are near zero (4% best, 0% for the rest); framework design drives energy, SLM reasoning limits success.
venue: Proceedings 2026 International Workshop on Agentic Engineering, AGENT 2026

title: Python 3 Using DeepSeek
methodology: Practitioner book covering DeepSeek's MoE architecture, Python programming, quantization and local deployment with Ollama.
results: No empirical study or benchmark results; descriptive tutorial content only.
venue: Python 3 Using DeepSeek

title: ViBench: A Benchmark on Vibe Coding
methodology: Benchmark construction for end-to-end web application development: 105 artifacts from 15 applications, user-facing requirements, REPL-based browser evaluator (99% step agreement over 1082 steps); nine models, five closed and four open-weight.
results: Best models Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.2 reach only 46% and 42% Pass@1; no open-weight model exceeds 12%; seven of nine degrade when extending their own code, with complete failure rates up to 40%.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems, CAIS 2026

title: Adaptive Test-Time Reasoning with Uncertainty-Guided Verification: Enhancing Intrinsic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models
methodology: Uncertainty-guided adaptive test-time reasoning with progressive verification and adaptive backtracking (ATR-UV); Llama-3.1-8B across GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, ASDiv, HumanEval and BBH.
results: +7.7% over Best-of-N on GSM8K and +6.5% over MCTS on MATH, with 38.7% fewer tokens and a 24.2% relative gain on problems needing seven or more steps.
venue: Proceedings of 2026 International Conference on Computer Intelligence and Software Engineering, CICSE 2026

title: MERIT: A Multi-Signal Repair Framework for Code Translation with Large Language Models
methodology: Multi-signal repair for code translation using AST comparison, a language knowledge base, error-pattern matching and self-reflection (MERIT); TransCoder and HumanEval-X, six directions, five LLMs.
results: Relative gains of 1.3-13.1% in compilation accuracy and 1.3-25.7% in execution accuracy; beats UniTrans by 3.0-3.6 pp on CodeLlama-7B.
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence and Software Engineering, ICBASE 2026

title: Closing the Loop: Code Generation and Intelligent Debugging with Large Language Models
methodology: Closed generate-execute-feedback loop with static and dynamic analysis, patch voting and early stopping; 4-bit quantization plus small MoE; Llama3-8B on HumanEval, DebugBench and LiveCodeBench.
results: About +7 percentage points on DebugBench; VRAM cut by roughly 32 GB to about 16 GB; returns turn negative around the third iteration.
venue: 2026 IEEE 18th International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks, CICN 2026

title: Evo-CuRL: Curriculum-Aware Reinforcement Learning over Code Lineage Graphs for Software Engineering Reasoning
methodology: Curriculum-aware reinforcement learning over code lineage graphs on a Llama-3 base; SWE-bench Verified and Lite.
results: 45.6% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified and 38.7% on Lite, state of the art among open-source models under 100B; ablations cost 2.5-3.8 pp.
venue: ICMR 2026 - Proceedings of the 16th ACM International Conference on Multimedia Retrieval

title: Energy Profiling of Pruned LLMs During Python Code Generation
methodology: Structured width pruning of Llama-3.2 1B/3B and Llama-3.1 8B, measuring HumanEval accuracy and GPU/CPU/DRAM energy with the Zeus library.
results: Pruning improves energy efficiency only up to a threshold; beyond it, pruned models can consume more energy than unpruned baselines.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th ACM International Green and Sustainable Computing Conference, IGSC 2026

title: Geometric prompt optimization: An efficient framework for engineering applications of large language models
methodology: Optimal-transport prompt optimization on probability manifolds; Qwen2.5 7B/72B and Llama-3 8B/70B on GSM8K, HumanEval, CommonsenseQA and BBH.
results: +7.2 pp (11.7% relative) over zero-shot and +2.2 pp over OPRO; +13.8% for 7-8B models; 73% cost reduction (3.0 vs 11.2 GPU-hours).
venue: Expert Systems with Applications

title: An Empirical Study of Reasoning Steps in Thinking Code LLMs
methodology: Empirical analysis of reasoning traces from six thinking LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Gemini-2.0/2.5-Flash, Qwen-QwQ) on 100 BigCodeBench tasks (600 instances, 3772 steps) plus a 21-participant human evaluation.
results: Completeness issues dominate failures (44.5%), mostly missed edge cases; the step-count/success relation is model- and difficulty-dependent and verbosity is not a reliable correctness signal.
venue: AIware 2026 - Proceedings of the 3rd ACM International Conference on AI-Powered Software, Co-located with FSE 2026

title: Prompt Optimization for LLM Code Generation via Reinforcement Learning
methodology: PPO agent for prompt refinement with a hybrid action space (generation, genetic mutation, semantic rewriting) and unit-test-shaped rewards; frozen CodeT5+, CodeLLaMA and DeepSeek-Coder on MBPP+, HumanEval+ and APPS.
results: MBPP+ strict Pass@1 of 57.58%, 64.80% and 85.50%; soft Pass@1 of 67.90%, 73.10% and 88.20%, beating EPiC, Reflexion and Random-Hybrid.
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science

title: BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored Co-Evolution of Code and Test Populations
methodology: Bayesian co-evolution of code and test populations with belief updates anchored on minimal public examples (BACE); LiveCodeBench v6 (post-March 2025), proprietary and 7B/120B open-weight models.
results: State-of-the-art results across both proprietary and open-weight models at 7B and 120B scales; no figures in the abstract.
venue: GECCO 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Trajectory Data Curation for LoRA Fine-Tuning of Code Agents
methodology: Systematic study of trajectory data curation for LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on 67,074 SWE trajectories, with 16 controlled experiments and cross-entropy loss as a validated proxy.
results: Doubling data from 500 to 1000 trajectories cuts CE loss by about 12.7%, while the quality-versus-random gap stays under 1% until 2000 trajectories (3.6%, p = 0.016); error-retry rate is the dominant quality sub-dimension.
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science

title: Do influence tactics matter? investigating prompt framing effects in LLM code generation
methodology: Eight influence-tactic prompt templates from Yukl and Falbe operationalized as reproducible prompts; five open-weight LLMs on LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench Verified, scored on correctness, quality, maintainability and security.
results: Urgency-oriented framings are associated with reduced correctness and security; other tactics show no consistent benefit. No figures in the abstract.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering

title: AlquistCoder: A Synthetic Data Approach to Training Compact Secure Coding Assistants and Building Security Benchmarks
methodology: Compact 3.8B assistant (Phi-4-mini) trained with SFT plus DPO on constitution-guided synthetic data; CyberSecEval, HumanEval, SecurityEval, VulnBench and MalBench.
results: Reduces statically detected vulnerabilities and judged malicious-assistance rates versus base and comparable baselines while keeping competitive coding performance.
venue: Computational Intelligence

title: Can LLMs Refactor Their Own Smelly Code? Self-Refactoring Effectiveness and Behavioral Preservation Across Four Open-Source Models
methodology: Taxonomy of six LLM-specific Python code smells (F1 = 0.87); self-refactoring of 1404 real-inference snippets from CodeLlama-13B, DeepSeekCoder-6.7B, StarCoder2-15B and Qwen2.5-Coder-14B on BigCodeBench, plus a cross-refactoring experiment.
results: 96.0% behavioral preservation rate (95% CI 93.3-97.7%); self-refactoring profiles range from 0% median success (CodeLlama) to 100% (DeepSeekCoder); self-refactoring never beats the best independent refactorer (0/89).
venue: Applied Sciences (Switzerland)

title: Large Language Models for Fault Localization: An Empirical Study
methodology: Systematic empirical study of statement-level fault localization with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4.1 mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash on HumanEval-Java and Defects4J, comparing zero-shot, few-shot and CoT against PMD and LineDef.
results: Bug-report context improves localization on Defects4J; few-shot gains are inconsistent and CoT effects are mixed across models; the study reports trade-offs rather than a single winner.
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOFTWARE ENGINEERING AND KNOWLEDGE ENGINEERING

title: Intelligent automated code review and software quality evaluation: a survey of AutoML and large language model techniques
methodology: Narrative survey of AutoML and LLM techniques for automated code review and software quality evaluation, covering 2020-2026 literature and benchmarks such as Defects4J, Big-Vul, CodeXGLUE and SWE-bench.
results: No new measurements; organizes the field by task taxonomy and sets out a six-point research agenda on scalability, generalization, explainability and trust calibration.
venue: AUTOMATED SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

title: Automated Program Repair using Quantized Language Models and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methodology: QLoRA (4-bit quantization plus LoRA) across CodeGen, InCoder, CodeLlama, StarCoder2 and Qwen2.5-Coder; Defects4J, QuixBugs and HumanEval-Java, measuring accuracy, latency and memory.
results: More plausible patches with less memory; within a 24 GB GPU budget, QLoRA enables larger models and 35% more plausible patches (some percentages masked in the abstract).
venue: Information and Software Technology

title: Distilling large language models for code generation via ranking supervision
methodology: Ranking-based knowledge distillation with a ListNet loss over teacher top-probability tokens; Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder families on HumanEval, MBPP, DS-1000 and MultiPL-E.
results: Consistently beats supervised fine-tuning and forward/reverse KL distillation across Python, multilingual and data-science tasks, with lower GPU memory and comparable training time.
venue: Neural Networks

title: Epistemic fortitude: Architectural specialization for sycophancy mitigation in software engineering agents
methodology: Multi-agent epistemic oversight architecture (primary agent plus arbiter agent, hybrid keyword/LLM router); 300 SWE-bench Lite conversations across Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Llama 3.3 70B (2400 conversations).
results: Statistically significant sycophancy reduction in all four model families; architectural separation explains 49-77% of the gain in low-baseline models, at modest token overhead.
venue: Information Processing and Management

title: Quantum assistant: Specialization of multimodal vision-language models for quantum computing
methodology: Multimodal Qiskit dataset (8366 samples, 45% with images) plus parameter-efficient VLM specialization (rsLoRA on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct) chosen from five LoRA variants; Qiskit HumanEval and Qiskit HumanEval Hard.
results: 41.72% and 30.46% Pass@1 versus 40.40%/25.83% for Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Qiskit and 17.88%/9.93% for granite-3.3-8b-qiskit; multimodal samples reach 64.29% versus 46.33% text-only.
venue: Expert Systems with Applications
